column1: # Ground truth for the chainlink #108 comparison, hand-verified against
# One row per true call edge in the P2 subset.  Columns:
#   2 cxx_caller C++ caller, named the way codesight-mcp names it
#   3 cxx_callee C++ callee, named the way codesight-mcp names it
#   4 cxx_site   file:line of the call in the pinned source
#   5 rust_*     the subset-port fixture's caller / callee, so ligature has
#                something to scan (this pilot has no crate yet).  A blank
#                rust_* means the fixture has no counterpart and the row counts
# The fixture is a transcription, so ligature "finding" an edge it was handed
# proves nothing; what this table measures is whether each tool *recovers* a
# C++ edge from its own input.  See not-found-absent.tsv and
# not-found-present.tsv (both derived by classify-not-found.py) for the symbols
# codesight-mcp reported as `Symbol not found`, split by whether they exist at
